chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) said: It was narrated to me by Abdullah ibn Ja'far from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar from his brother Ali ibn Mahziyar from Ibn Abi Umayr from Mansur ibn Yunis from Muhammad ibn Marwan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

There is nothing that does not have a measure and a weight except tears, for indeed a drop of them extinguishes a sea of fire. And when the eye is filled with its water, no soot or disgrace covers his face. And when they flow, Allah prohibits the Fire upon it. And even if one person weeps, the whole community is dealt with mercy.

key_terms.بِحَاراً: A sea (metaphor for a vast amount)
key_terms.قَتَر: Soot (metaphor for the mark of sin or neglect)

ai.seo_question: What is the reward of weeping in the fear of Allah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this tradition to emphasize the unique ontological status of tears as a spiritual currency exempt from the usual cosmic measures (kayl wa wazn). The narration underscores the transformative power of sincere weeping, noting that it not only extinguishes Hellfire but also preserves the believer's dignity by preventing the 'soot' of sin from darkening their countenance. This reflects the Shia emphasis on emotional piety (khushu') as a tangible means of intercession and purification.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. My father (rah) said: it was narrated to me by Abdillah b. Ja’far from Ibrahim b. Mahziyar from his brother Ali b. Mahziyar from Ibn Abi ’Umayr from Mansur b. Yunis from Muhammad b. Marwan from Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “

There is nothing but that it has a measure and a weight except the tears. For indeed a drop of it can extinguish a sea of fire. And when ones eyes are filled with tears, his face will never see poverty or disgrace. And when tears are flowing, Allah prohibits the fire of Hell on it and even if one person is weeping the whole community is dealt with mercy (by Allah).”
